title: CI setup-python pins: change a micro-version together with the test fixtures that hard-code it
answers: Why do sklearn or virtualenv model tests fail after the CI Python version pin changed?
Where do I update the Python micro version used in CI for Python 3.10 or 3.11 on Linux, macOS, or Windows?
Which test resource files and assertions hard-code a Python patch version like 3.10.21 or 3.11.16?
How do I bump the pinned Python version used by MLflow CI jobs without breaking model export tests?
body:
Path: .github/actions/setup-python/action.yml (composite action, PIN_MICRO_VERSION block) maps the requested major.minor Python (3.10, 3.11, 3.12) to a per-OS micro version, which every CI job using this action installs.
Rule: when a pin changes, update in the same PR the companion fixtures that record or assert that version: tests/resources/example_*/python_env.yaml, conda.yaml (python=...), MLmodel python_version, the sys.version_info assertion in entrypoint.py files, and inline YAML in tests/sklearn/test_sklearn_model_export.py (test_sklearn_compatible_with_mlflow_2_4_0). This follows the convention from #23684.
Symptom: after a pin change without matching fixtures, model-export and virtualenv/conda environment tests compare against a stale patch version and fail.
Constraints: the pins follow each runner image's hosted toolcache, so Linux, macOS and Windows can legitimately differ (e.g. 3.11.16 on Linux, 3.11.9 on macOS and Windows). Does not apply to runtime MLflow code or to 3.12 entries.
applies: CI GitHub Actions pins for setup-python and the sklearn/virtualenv test fixtures that hard-code Python patch versions.
says: Model export tests are failing due to a mismatch in the recorded environment version.
Virtual environment tests fail when checking the installed runtime patch version against saved metadata.
Update model artifact test fixtures whenever the continuous integration runtime patch version is upgraded.
Packaged machine learning models fail compatibility checks against previous releases after pipeline updates.
Why do model serialization tests fail expecting an older runtime patch release?
search: When changing a Python micro-version pin in .github/actions/setup-python/action.yml PIN_MICRO_VERSION, companion test fixtures hard-coding that patch version must be updated in the same pull request. Required fixture updates include python_env.yaml, conda.yaml, MLmodel python_version, sys.version_info in entrypoint.py, and inline YAML in tests/sklearn/test_sklearn_model_export.py (test_sklearn_compatible_with_mlflow_2_4_0). Failing to synchronize pins and fixtures causes model-export and virtualenv/conda environment tests to compare against stale patch versions and fail. Pins track hosted toolcaches and may differ across Linux, macOS, and Windows; the rule does not apply to 3.12 entries or runtime MLflow code.
